QUESTION: As of August 25, 2005, what is the simplified KYC procedure for opening accounts for individuals who intend to keep balances not exceeding Rs.50, 000 in all their accounts taken together, according to the RBI circular mentioned in the document?

RESPONSE:
chosen:

According to [rbi:rbi_notifications:2459 / para 1], banks are required to formulate a customer acceptance policy and customer identification procedure to be followed while opening an account. The 'Know Your Customer' guidelines also require banks to verify the identity and address of the customer through documents listed in Annex II to the circular.

However, it has been brought to the RBI's notice that a large number of persons, especially those belonging to the low-income group, are not able to produce documents to satisfy the bank about their identity and address. To simplify the KYC procedure, the RBI has decided to allow persons who intend to keep balances not exceeding Rs.50, 000 in all their accounts taken together and the total credits in all the accounts to open accounts without requiring the documents listed in Annex II. This decision is effective as of the date of the circular, which is August 23, 2005.

Therefore, as of August 23, 2005, banks are required to follow the simplified KYC procedure for opening accounts for persons who intend to keep balances not exceeding Rs.50, 000 in all their accounts taken together and the total credits in all the accounts.

No. 60/ 02.01 / 2005-06 dated December 9, 2005 [rbi:rbi_notifications:2659 / para 1], all deposit accounts standing to the credit of sole/first named depositor in the same capacity shall be clubbed and treated as one deposit account for the purpose of premature repayment.

This clause is applicable in case of problem NBFC/RNBC/MNBC only, as clarified in the amending Notifications Nos. 182-184 of date [rbi:rbi_notifications:2659 / para 2]. Any income generated from investments made with this fund must also be reinvested back into the same fund [sebi:sebi_circulars:42427 / para 2]. Exchanges are mandated to follow specific guiding principles for the utilization of this earmarked fund [sebi:sebi_circulars:42427 / para 3].

It is worth noting that the RBI has also announced that payment systems, including RTGS, will remain open on Saturdays and Sundays [RBI/2016-17/116 / para 1]. However, this provision does not specifically relate to the implementation of the positive confirmation feature in the RTGS system.

- No UCB should appoint any other UCB/entity as its sub-agent [rbi:rbi_notifications:3724 / para 1].
